motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the addition of “trails” under Article II, Scope of Review, on Item 13.C. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, with trails added
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, adding "trails" to the scope of review in one of the items it covered.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping — the consent agenda bundles uncontested items into one vote, and nothing here changes for residents.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #45:326:0109, Designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 as presented in the packet and including the following: • Setting the price at $2.07 sq/foo t; and • The applicant will bear all costs associated with the item, including survey fees and any other fees related to the disposition
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #45:326:0109, Designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 as presented in the packet and including the following: • Setting the price at $2.07 sq/foo t; and • The applicant will bear all costs associated with the item, including survey fees and any other fees related to the disposition . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City land sold at $2.07 a square foot
motions.summary: The city approved selling part of a city-owned parcel in Utah County at $2.07 per square foot, with the buyer paying all related costs.
motions.impact: Most residents will notice nothing. The buyer covers the survey and other fees, so the sale costs the city nothing and moves a piece of public land into private hands.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Pledge of any portion of the City’s Sales and Use Taxes to the Proposed Issuance of the Redevelopment Agency’s Sales Tax and Tax Increment Revenue Bonds, Series 2026 (the “Bonds” ) and Authorizing the Execution of Related Pledge and Bond Documents Thereto and all other Actions Required to Pledge Sales and Use Taxes to the Bonds.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Pledge of any Portion of the City’s Sales and Use Taxes to the Proposed Issuance of the Redevelopment Agency’s Sales Tax ad Tax Increment Revenue Bonds, Series 2026 (the “Bonds”) and Authorizing the Execution of Related Pledge and Bond Documents Thereto and all other Actions Required to Pledge Sales and Use Taxes to the Bonds. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sales tax pledged to back redevelopment bonds
motions.summary: The council took up a resolution pledging part of the city's sales tax revenue to repay bonds the city's redevelopment agency plans to issue in 2026.
motions.impact: No new tax and no bill for you. The city would be promising some of its sales tax income to bondholders, money that would otherwise be free for other city spending.

motions.item_title: Add evaluation of speed bumps and speed tables be added to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to add evaluation of speed bumps and speed tables be added to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Speed bumps added to council's study list
motions.summary: The council added an evaluation of speed bumps and speed tables to its Legislative Priorities List.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on your street. This only puts the question of speed bumps and speed tables on the council's list of things to look at later.
